name: Note Studio
description: Local-first Markdown notes and quick records with AI assistance: file workspace, WYSIWYG editor, tags, full-text search and streaming chat.
releaseNotes: First listing. Local-first Markdown workbench shipped as a DBX plugin: the workspace is a plain folder of .md files, edited WYSIWYG or in source mode. Records, tags, chats and settings live in the plugin's own SQLite database. The Rust sidecar owns every privileged operation (files, SQLite, AI HTTP/SSE, GDI screen capture with a native 1:1 region selector and in-place annotation, clipboard bitmaps, microphone recording), so the plugin page itself has no file or network access. v0.4.0 hardens the editor: in-note search and replace (Ctrl+F, match counter, replace all, match case), GitHub alert callouts (NOTE/TIP/IMPORTANT/WARNING/CAUTION) that round-trip through Markdown, a rebuilt table toolbar (row/column/align/delete groups, disabled states, active alignment) with tooltips that no longer cover the header, and a full shortcut set for tables, math, Mermaid and heading collapse. v0.5.0 rebuilds AI configuration around providers and models: several providers can coexist (presets for OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, Zhipu, Moonshot, SiliconFlow, OpenRouter, Groq, Together, xAI, Ollama, LM Studio), models are fetched from the provider with one click, each model carries its own type, temperature, top_p, max_tokens and streaming flag, and chat / image recognition / speech transcription can each point at a different model. Existing single-model settings are migrated automatically, and a chat-model fallback keeps recognition working for users who only configured one multimodal model. It also fixes cloud sync treating a workspace that merely sits inside another repository as an initialized repo, which could have committed notes into the parent repository. v0.5.1 makes Git sync compare files individually on open, pull one note at a time, surface real conflicts and refresh the editor after a pull. v0.5.2 completes that alignment with the reference implementation: entering the file tree or returning to the app fetches a remote directory listing, remote-only notes show up in the sidebar with a cloud icon and their content is downloaded only when opened; the auto-sync interval now controls pushing only, so it no longer disables pull-on-open. The global screenshot selector gains eight resize handles with native double-arrow cursors, and in-place annotations, toolbar and final output all follow the resized region. Also included: throttled remote listing refresh, serialized settings persistence, and a guard against a nested workspace reading its parent Git repository. v0.5.3 adds the editor footer bar from the reference implementation: copy the current note as Markdown, HTML, JSON or plain text; export it as Markdown, HTML, JSON or PDF (system print dialog, with an HTML fallback when printing is blocked); an outline toggle and a live character count. A new local version history is written to SQLite on every save (deduplicated, at most one automatic snapshot per minute, 50 per note), with manual checkpoints, full-text preview and a two-step restore that first saves the current draft so the operation stays reversible. History works offline and needs no cloud sync. Clipboard writes also get a longer retry window on Windows. v0.5.4 corrects both footer features to match the reference implementation exactly. Exports now open a native Save As dialog, write to the path the user picks and report that path back in the UI; cancelling writes nothing and shows no success message (browser download is only a fallback on platforms without a native dialog). JSON export is a Tiptap JSON document and HTML exports inline workspace images as data URLs so files stay self-contained. Version history is no longer a local snapshot list: it shows the last ten commits for the current note from the configured GitHub / Gitee / GitLab / Gitea remote, with short SHA links, commit message, author, date, an open-in-repository link and restore-by-commit; the entry is hidden entirely when no Git remote is configured. v0.5.5 fixes two export defects: all four formats now keep their own extension (the Save As dialog no longer reuses the previous .html filter, and the target path is normalized from the requested format), and the native Save As dialog is forced to the foreground by binding the host window as owner plus a topmost hook. PDF printing now uses a top-level window so the plugin iframe sandbox cannot swallow it, and falls back to a clearly named .print.html file instead of a silent ordinary HTML export. It also completes the file-tree note operations from the reference implementation: a More menu with sorting by name / modified time / size, collapse all, toggles for asset folders, knowledge-base status and remote files, local / Markdown / Notion .zip imports, remote file upload and download, and knowledge-base index rebuild and snapshot export / import; plus a context menu with new file / folder, expand / collapse, reveal in file manager, create from template, knowledge-base actions, cut / copy / duplicate / paste with Ctrl+X/C/V, folder upload / download, rename (F2) and delete (Del). Sorting and view toggles persist in settings, shortcuts only fire while the file tree has focus, and the knowledge-base actions map to a workspace .dbx-note/kb-index.json index snapshot that travels with cloud sync.
